definition: Bit 15 of SimEvent.flags. The record continues the event before it: it holds that event's arguments 7 to 12. It is clear in a first record.
kit_reference: layout.json SimEvent.flags; interfaces/services.h SIM_EVENT_CONTINUED; the section The record

definition: Bit 0 of SimEvent.flags, used by SIM_EVENT_UNIT_SPEECH only: the line is spoken only while the unit is off screen.
The unit is alive: its slot of the unit table holds a unit. Set when the unit is created, cleared when it is removed. Unit.flags is the 32-bit word at offset 272, and this is its bit 28.

The unit is dying: the next unit pass kills it with a kill type equal to the damage kind held in Unit.lastDamageType at that time (the kind of its last damage, or 7 for a finished isfeature unit). A dying unit takes no further damage and records no speech. Bit 14 of Unit.flags. Every writer: (1) damage of a kind that takes health (every kind but 2 and 10) that takes the health of a unit of an active player of type 1 or 2 to 0 or below sets it (for a unit of any other player the health is clamped to 0 and the unit is not marked); (2) a unit whose definition has isfeature (bit 24 of UnitDef.flags1) gets it, with last damage type 7, when its construction finishes and when it is created already finished; (3) a network unit state that says the slot of an existing unit is empty sets it (the kill type is then whatever Unit.lastDamageType holds); (4) when all the units of a player are removed (a commander's death under the commander-death rule, a player leaving a network game, the console commands), the units of a player that is not active or not of type 1 or 2 get it just before they are killed at once with kill type 3 (the units of an active player of type 1 or 2 take damage kind 3 instead); (5) a saved game restores it.

The unit is a structure: its definition is not mobile, so it has no motion and stays where it stands. Bit 29 of Unit.flags. The pseudo-unit that the feature pool keeps for features (it has no unit definition and belongs to no player) also has the bit, set when the pool is created.

Display flags of a unit for the radar of the viewed player (the player this machine views). Bits 8 and 9 of Unit.flags. They are recomputed in the 30-tick update of the viewed player, in four steps; with fewer than 2 players nothing runs. Step 1: every unit that exists gets both bits when it belongs to the viewed player, or when its player is allied to the viewed player and shares radar (the share radar flag, 0x40, of that player's start information), or when the viewed player is active and in watch mode (info flag 0x40); every other unit gets both bits, and bit 10 (0x400), cleared. Step 2: each unit of the viewed player that exists, is not dying and is switched on (activation bit 0), and has a radar or a sonar distance, marks the units of other players inside the larger of the two distances, skipping a unit whose definition has the stealth flag (bit 8 of UnitDef.flags1): 0x100 (radar) when the top of the target (its position plus the height of its model) is at or above sea level and it is inside the radar distance, which is the definition's radar distance plus twice the sensor's whole height; 0x200 (sonar) when the target is at or below sea level and inside the sonar distance. Step 3: each unit that exists, is switched on and belongs to any player but the viewed one (an ally included) clears 0x100 on every unit inside its radar jamming distance, and 0x200 on every unit inside its sonar jamming distance, and sets 0x400 on them; the jammer's own unit and the viewed player's own units are cleared like any other. Step 4: every unit that exists, is not cloaked (activation bit 2 clear) and has 0x100 clear gets 0x100 when the viewed player sees its position (explored when map flag 2 is set, else visible), so a jammed unit that is seen and not cloaked has 0x100 again, while its 0x200 stays cleared. This depends on the local viewer: the bits of one unit differ between machines that view different players, and the simulation reads them (the visibility test of a unit below sea level reads 0x200, and the list of known enemy units of an AI player reads 0x100), so a machine whose viewer differs can give an AI player different lists.

definition: The unit is switched on. Gaining it makes the unit run its activate script and say the activate line, losing it the deactivate script and line. Bit 0 of Unit.activateFlags.
The unit is cloaked. Gaining it says the cloak line, losing it the uncloak line. Bit 2 (value 4) of Unit.activateFlags.

Bit 7 of the flags word of the unit's first order (Order.flags_42). An order copies the word from the order table entry of its kind when it is made (an entry holds the kind's marker animation in one byte and, right after it, this 32-bit flags word). The entries of Attack no move, Attack chase and Attack special have bit 7 set, and no other entry has it. Nothing else sets or clears it, except an order that changes its kind and so takes the word of the entry of its new kind (Attack special on its step, and the park order of an air unit, which keep only bits 0x200 and 0x400 of the old word). It is tested at the end of the reaction to an attack: a unit whose first order has it set (one of the three attack kinds) records no underattack line; a unit with no orders has the bit clear. So the test does not always pass; the other conditions of the line are in the speech section.

Bit 13 of Order.flags_42. It is set on an order added without the queue modifier: the add-order call is made with its remove argument 0, so the order replaces the unit's unprotected orders. The interface passes 1 when the queue key is held (the plus of the scenario format), and mission scripts and the changes of a build queue pass 1. The AI passes 0 for most of its orders and 1 for the order that sends a unit back to its origin. No entry of the order table has the bit, so this call is its only setter. An order that takes the word of a new kind (Attack special on its step, the park order of an air unit) loses it. The word is saved with the order. The only test of it is the announce step: the first step of an announcing order that finds it set clears it and records the ok speech (slot 5) with the order's text, so an order announces once.

definition: A call flag (0x2) of an order step: the order is being removed from the unit's list. Removing an order destroys it, and its destructor calls its step one last time with this flag whenever the order's wake mask has bit 1 (value 2) set at that moment. That covers an order cancelled before it finished and an order that finished: a step that returns 5 or 8 has the order removed, and the last step of a help-build order sets the bit as it returns 5, so it is called with the flag after it finished. An order is called with a flag only when it asked for it in its wake mask.

definition: A call flag (0x8) of an order step: a unit the order refers to has been removed (killed or freed). The steps of the build orders treat it as the stop of construction and say the construction stopped or terminated line.

definition: A call flag of an order step: the movement goal of the order reports that the unit has arrived inside the goal. The goal sets it with its flag word when the unit stands in the goal area.

definition: A ground pickup order (the order that loads a unit into a transport) runs by Order.state. State 0 checks that the transport can carry and that the unit fits. State 1 waits until the transport's script is idle. State 2 starts a pickup attempt: it runs the transport's pickup script, records the load speech, counts the attempt in the order's attempts and waits 15 ticks. State 3 waits until the script is idle. State 4 ends the order if the unit is now carried (by any carrier); otherwise, with 3 or more attempts counted, it gives up (the result 9); otherwise it sends the transport to the unit and waits for its arrival. Giving up deletes the order only when another order follows it; with none following, the order waits 30 ticks and restarts at state 0 without resetting the attempts count, so it goes through states 1 to 4 again, state 2 counts one more attempt, and state 4 gives up again unless the unit is carried. State 5 drops that goal and starts again at state 0.

State 2 of a stockpile order (the order that builds a weapon's stockpile) is the last step of one stockpiled weapon: it adds 1 to the slot's stockpile and takes 1 from the order's count, then the order starts again at state 0. State 0 ends the order when its count is 0 or less, waits 300 ticks while the stockpile is at 200 and otherwise clears the progress. State 1 pays the reload cost in steps of 5 ticks of progress, from the economy, until the progress reaches the weapon's reload time.

Bit 0 of Game.mapFlags. When a match starts, the visibility mask starts all clear if this bit is set (unmapped) and all set if it is clear (mapped). The options screen shows Unmapped when it is set and Mapped when it is clear. The radar snapshot of units is enabled only when this bit and map flag 2 are both clear, unless match flag 2 is set. Both bits are cleared for a local player in watch mode.

Bit 1 of Game.mapFlags. When a match starts, each player's explored map starts all 0 if this bit is set and all 1 if it is clear. With it set, the tests of whether a player sees a position (units, projectiles, particles, sounds, the radar picture) read the player's explored map entry, which is non-zero for an explored cell; with it clear they read the visibility mask of the cell or the point visibility of the position. The options screen shows line of sight as Permanent when the bit is clear, and as True (bit 2 set) or Circular (bit 2 clear) when it is set. It is cleared for a local player in watch mode.

Bit 1 of Game.matchFlags, which is bit 9 of Game.uiOptionFlags (the same memory). The console command radar toggles it, and the start of a match clears it; nothing else sets it. When it is set, the radar snapshot of units is enabled whatever the map flags are.

Bit 0 of Game.netGameFlags: the front end has opened a network connection. It is set when the front end opens one (the connection to a service, or to a lobbied game, or to a game entered by address), before the player hosts or joins anything, and again in the battle room's leave step just before the game is quit; it is not set by hosting or joining as such. It is cleared whenever the main menu frame is set up or the game returns to the main menu, and when a mission is started from the end-of-game screen; nothing else writes it.

Bit 6 of the flags of a player's start information: the player is in watch mode. A defeated player of a network game is placed in it when the host allows watching or an AI player is active. In the lobby it is also set for a player who joins as a watcher, and on the slot of a human player when its side button is pressed past the last side while the host's watching option is on; it is cleared when the side button of a slot that has it is pressed, and when the player turns its own watching option off. For the local player it clears map flags 1 and 2, so it sees the whole map.

Bit 0 of the flags byte of a spot (an entry of the feature pool, which the cells of a placed feature refer to). A spot is an animation slot of the pool: one is made for a feature with a 3D object when it is placed, for a feature that burns, and for a feature that dies with a death animation; a feature without a 3D object has no spot until it burns or dies. The bit is set on the spot made for a burning feature and clear on the spot of a 3D-object feature and on a death animation, so set means the feature is burning.
The weapon does not show on radar. Bit 6 of WeaponDef.flags.

Bits 29 and 30 of WeaponDef.flags: the weapon is targetable by interceptors (0x20000000) or is an interceptor (0x40000000). The radar shows a projectile of such a weapon as the second kind (a nuclear one), and any other as an ordinary one.

term: definition's flag 4 of the second flags byte
definition: Bit 2 (value 4) of UnitDef.flags2: the unit can be switched on and off. A unit that cannot be switched shows its ranges always.
A number of the script command that emits an effect from a piece: a puff of white smoke at the piece (SIM_EVENT_WHITE_SMOKE). The numbers 0 to 5 of the same command are the vehicle trails.
A number of the script command that emits an effect from a piece: a puff of black smoke at the piece (SIM_EVENT_BLACK_SMOKE).
A number of the script command that emits an effect from a piece: bubbles that rise from the piece to the sea level (SIM_EVENT_BUBBLES).

The values 0xfffb to 0xffff of Cell.feature are markers and not numbers of a feature (0xffff is no feature, 0xfffe is a cell covered by a feature whose origin is another cell). A feature number is below 0xfffb.
A death by an ordinary weapon hit: the kill type of a unit killed by damage is the damage kind of its last damage, and kind 1 is the weapon hit.

A death by self-destruct, of a unit of a defeated player, or of the cargo of a transport that died with kill type 3. The damage of a self-destruct is damage kind 3. The death explosion uses the unit's self-destruct weapon in place of its ordinary death weapon.

A death by reclaim: the unit was being reclaimed, and the reclaim damage is damage kind 5. No death script runs, there is no death explosion and no wreck, and the unit's last attacker is paid the metal of the finished part of the unit.
A death of the cargo of a transport that was killed with any kill type but 3: the cargo takes damage kind 6 and so dies with kill type 6.

A quiet kill. A unit whose definition has isfeature (bit 24 of UnitDef.flags1) gets last damage type 7 and the dying flag 0x4000 when its construction finishes and when it is created already finished; the next unit pass then kills it with kill type 7, so such a unit disappears as soon as it is complete, with the wreck of level 1 described below. No damage call passes damage kind 7. The kill code handles it: the unit's death script is not run and its severity is 0, so there is no death explosion, and wreck level 1 is requested, but the wreck is made without the wreck smoke plume.

An ordinary weapon hit. It takes the amount from the unit's health. When that makes a unit of an active player of type 1 or 2 dying (health 0 or below, flag 0x4000 set), the hit ends there and neither the hit script nor the damage script runs. Otherwise (for a unit of any other player the health is clamped to 0) it runs the unit's hit script, with the direction of the hit, and then its damage script, with the health percent from 0 to 100. Every kind but 10 also marks the unit as recently damaged, sets its last damage type to the kind and, when the damage names an attacker, sets its last attacker and attacker slot; every kind but 10 and 11 runs the reaction to an attack first. The other kinds but 2 and 10 only take the amount from the health (and can make a unit dying in the same way) and run no script.

Paralysis (a paralyzer weapon). Its amount is a number of ticks and it takes no health. The tick count is the amount after the armour scaling that every damage call but kind 10 applies: (25 minus the armour) times the amount times 4, divided by 100, where the armour is the kill count of the target divided by 5, at most 5 (first, while the target's activation bit 1 is set and the amount is below 30000, the amount is multiplied by the definition's damage modifier and divided by 65536). The paralysis is added only on the machine that simulates the unit: when the unit's player is active and of type 1 or 2 and the definition is not immune to paralyzers (bit 26 of UnitDef.flags1). If the unit's first order is a paralyze order, the ticks are added to its tick count; otherwise a new paralyze order with the ticks is put at the front of the unit's orders and becomes its first order. For a unit of a player of type 3 nothing of this happens here: only the common effects of damage (the recently damaged mark, the last damage type and attacker) are applied on this machine, and the damage call sends the damage (every kind but 11) to the machine that owns the unit, where the paralysis is applied. An implementation that applied the paralysis on every machine would make the machines differ.
Healing: its amount is added to the unit's health up to its maximum, and nothing else happens (no reaction, no last damage, no last attacker).

Damage by the water: the damage of the match's water setting, once in 30 ticks, to a unit at or below the sea level that cannot float. It does not trigger the reaction to an attack and is not sent to other machines.
The match plays one mission of a campaign. The kit's name for it is the scenario key game_type with the value 1.
kit_reference: docs/scenario-format.md, the key game_type and section 3.3

definition: The match is a skirmish: the menu match against computer players. The kit's name for it is the scenario key game_type with the value 2.

definition: A human player whose orders this machine takes from its own input and whose units this machine simulates. The slot's controller is human. Orders, damage and deaths of its units are applied here, and the kills are sent to the other machines.

definition: A computer player that this machine runs: it has an AI manager that gives its units orders, and its units are simulated here like those of type 1. The slot's controller is ai, and the difficulty setting scales the metal it gets back from a cancelled or reclaimed build.

definition: A player on another machine. This machine does not run its orders or its AI: it applies the packets that arrive for it, and damage dealt to its units is sent to the machine that owns them. PlayerInfo.kind of the slot says what controls it there: 1 human, 2 computer.
